extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: TravelPlanner is a planning benchmark focused on travel planning that provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries, various tools for accessing data records, and 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans. It evaluates language agents' ability to handle complex multi-constraint planning tasks involving tool use, information collection, and decision making.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su (Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from multiple publicly available Internet sources including Kaggle datasets and Google APIs. The original data was then modified (adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values) to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Flight data from Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset (2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01); driving distance/time from Google Distance Matrix API; restaurant data from Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset; attraction data from Google Places API; accommodation data from Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Flight prices were generated by multiplying distance by a random factor ranging from 0.2 to 0.5. Restaurant data was randomly assigned to various cities and randomly categorized under cuisine types. Accommodation items were randomly assigned to various cities and assigned random room rules. Self-driving and taxi prices were calculated by multiplying distance by factors of 1 and 0.15 respectively.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For FlightSearch, specific fields were extracted (FlightDate, DepTime, ArrTime, ActualElapsedTime, Distance, OriginCityName, DestCityName) while discarding others. For DistanceMatrix, search results were stored in a fixed database. For AttractionSearch, essential details (Name, Address, Phone, Website, Latitude, Longitude) were retained. Query budgets were re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans to replace heuristic-generated budgets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan was deemed eligible only if it met all constraints outlined in the evaluation script. Annotators were paid an average of $0.80 per plan. Authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control was performed by the authors who reviewed every query and plan, rectifying any errors. Multiple stages of human verification were conducted to ensure high quality and the presence of at least one feasible solution per query.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4-Turbo (used for key component extraction from natural language plans during evaluation)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Evaluation scripts will be released. Use of evaluation feedback in training set is encouraged (e.g., reinforcement learning). Any form of cheating in validation and test sets is strictly prohibited.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The commonsense constraints are based on the authors' consensus, which may not reflect universal definitions of commonsense. The evaluation criteria may be biased toward the authors' viewpoints.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark uses a static and closed sandbox environment, which may not fully reflect the dynamic nature of real-world travel planning. The commonsense constraints are based on authors' consensus and may not capture all aspects of commonsense. Some data in the environment is derived from publicly available Internet data and the content does not represent the authors' viewpoints.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking and evaluating language agents on complex multi-constraint planning tasks involving tool use. It includes training (45 query-plan pairs), validation (180 queries), and test (1,000 queries) splits. The training set evaluation feedback can be used for reinforcement learning. Cheating on validation and test sets is strictly prohibited.

name.evidence: We propose TravelPlanner, a new planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning, a common real-world planning scenario.

description.evidence: TravelPlanner provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries crawled from the Internet that can be accessed via six tools. We also meticulously curate 1,225 diverse user queries (along with their reference plans), each imposing a different combination of constraints.

inLanguage.evidence: we utilize GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) to generate natural language queries.

isLiveDataset.evidence: In TravelPlanner, we create a static and closed sandbox environment for consistent and unbiased evaluations. This setup ensures that all agents access the same unchanging information from our static databases, avoiding the variability and potential biases introduced by dynamic data.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The original data for each tool is sourced from publicly available Internet data. We then modify this data, which includes adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit our requirements. In this way, we effectively avoid the problem of data contamination.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: For FlightSearch, we source original data from the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset... We utilize the Google Distance Matrix API to calculate the driving distance... For AttractionSearch, we employ the Google Places API to gather information about attractions in each city... Our restaurant data is sourced from the Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset... Our accommodation data is obtained from the Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: To ensure the quality of each natural language query and its corresponding annotated plan, the authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found... rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We will release our evaluation scripts to foster innovation and aid the development of new methods. We encourage the use of evaluation feedback in training set, such as implementing reinforcement learning techniques, to enhance learning. However, we strictly prohibit any form of cheating in the validation and test sets to uphold the fairness and reliability of the benchmark's evaluation process.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We realize that everyone's definition of commonsense may be different. Our current evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus, and we encourage additional discussions to enrich our commonsense dimension, aiming for a more thorough evaluation.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: In TravelPlanner, we create a static and closed sandbox environment for consistent and unbiased evaluations... Some of the data in the TravelPlanner environment is derived from publicly available data on the Internet, and the content involved does not represent the authors' viewpoints. We realize that everyone's definition of commonsense may be different.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: TravelPlanner comprises 1,225 queries in total... The training set includes 5 queries per group with human-annotated plans (45 pairs in total), the validation set includes 20 queries per group (180 in total), and the test set includes 1,000 queries... We encourage the use of evaluation feedback in training set, such as implementing reinforcement learning techniques, to enhance learning. However, we strictly prohibit any form of cheating in the validation and test sets.
